Bird.title: Bird
Bird.description: Represents a virtual duck resident in the Decent Ducks Sanctuary, holding all core profile information and AI-generated lore.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Bird entity.

name.description: The common name of the duck resident.

breed.description: The breed or species of the duck resident.

sex.description: The biological sex of the duck resident (e.g., Male, Female, Unknown).

heritageTree.description: A descriptive string representing the visual lineage or heritage information of the duck.

eggCounter.description: A counter tracking the number of eggs laid by the duck, manageable by administrators.

personalityTraits.description: AI-generated rich, unique personality traits for the duck, enhancing virtual adoption appeal.

backstory.description: AI-generated compelling backstory and lore for the duck.

primaryImageUrl.description: URL for the primary image displayed for the duck on dashboards and profiles.

galleryImageUrls.description: An array of URLs for additional images in the duck's photo gallery, uploaded via Firebase Storage.

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the bird's profile was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the bird's profile was last updated.

HealthLogEntry.title: HealthLogEntry
HealthLogEntry.description: Records dated health notes for a specific bird resident, accessible via the admin dashboard.

id.description: Unique identifier for the HealthLogEntry entity.

birdId.description: Reference to the Bird entity this health log pertains to. (Relationship: Bird 1:N HealthLogEntry)

logDate.description: The date and time when the health note was recorded.

notes.description: Detailed health notes or observations for the bird.

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the health log entry was created.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to be secure, scalable, and debuggable, adhering strictly to the core design principles and strategy mandates. 

**Authorization Independence (CRITICAL) and QAPs:**

1.  **Global Admin Role (`/roles_admin/{uid}`):** To ensure Authorization Independence and support DBAC, administrator roles are managed in a top-level collection (`/roles_admin`). A document's existence at `/roles_admin/{request.auth.uid}` grants admin privileges. This completely isolates authorization logic from data documents, eliminating the need for `get()` operations in security rules to determine a user's role. This pattern is inherently QAP-compliant because rules can verify admin status atomically and efficiently for any read or write operation across other collections.

2.  **Publicly Readable Bird Data (`/birds/{birdId}`):** The `Bird` collection stores all virtual duck resident profiles. This collection is designed for public read access (for dashboards and profiles) and admin-only write access (for management). This homogeneous security posture simplifies rules: any user can read, and only authenticated users with an existing document in `/roles_admin/{uid}` can create, update, or delete. This supports QAPs for public `list` operations without requiring client-side filtering or complex server-side logic.

3.  **Admin-Only Health Logs (`/birds/{birdId}/health_logs/{healthLogId}`):** Health log entries are stored as a subcollection under `Bird`. While logically nested, the security posture for this subcollection is *not* dependent on specific fields within the parent `Bird` document (e.g., an `ownerId` on the bird). Instead, access for `HealthLogEntry` documents is *exclusively* granted to administrators, as verified by the `/roles_admin` collection. The `birdId` field within each `HealthLogEntry` document ensures referential integrity and facilitates querying but is not used for authorization. This design achieves Authorization Independence because the security rule for `health_logs` only needs to check the global admin role, not the parent `Bird` document's data. This also makes `list` operations QAP-compliant, as an admin can list all health logs for a bird, and non-admins cannot list any.

**Denormalization:**

*   No complex denormalization of authorization context is required for `Bird` or `HealthLogEntry` documents because access is either public (for Bird reads) or determined by a global admin role. The `HealthLogEntry`'s `birdId` is part of its schema, providing the necessary link without needing parent document reads for authorization.
